iso_allergenicity: Sera were collected from 107 patients during the Artemisia ordosica pollen season. Allergic patients were selected based on typical clinical symptoms of allergic rhinitis, a self-reported history of allergy to A. ordosica and sIgE to A. ordosica extract measured by ELISA. A control group of 50 healthy subjects without any symptoms of allergic rhinitis and no known allergy to A. ordosica pollen was included. IgE from 98 of 107 (92%) allergic patients' sera and 3 of 50 (6%) control sera bound to recombinant Art o 11.0101, expressed in E. coli. The recombinant allergen inhibited IgE binding to A. ordosica pollen extract by up to 73% using a pool of Art o 11.0101-positive sera.

Of those, 13 sera were then tested in immunoblots to check IgE binding to collagen from specific fish species and for specific collagen alpha chains.   Of 13 sera tested in immunoblot, IgE from 11 bound to collagen alpha 1 and alpha 2 chains from both muscle and skin tissue of Atlantic salmon.   In addition, basophil activation test was performed with whole blood of one of the collagen-sensitized patients and one negative control, using salmon muscle collagen as stimulant of basophils. The result was positive for the collagen-sensitized patient and negative for the negative control.  As negative controls, 3 non-atopic individuals without history of type I allergy and 2 atopic individuals with allergies other than fish were used for ELISA and immunoblots. One atopic control was used in basophil activation test.

iso_allergenicity: The taxonomy of Arthroderma and Trichophyton is a bit messy. [Arthroderma benhamiae (anamorph: Trichophyton mentagrophytes]. Tri m 4, Tri r 4 and Tri t 4 appear to be homologues that are close. These proteins seem to be important in IgE mediated and DTH responses in those with skin or nail fungal infections who are also IgE sensitized and experience immediate responses. Woodfolk has a very good review in 2005, and also specific IgE binding in 1998.      The Woodfolk 1996 article used sera from 30 subjects with SPT + tests to Hollister-Stier's Trichophyton mixture (T. tonsurans, T. rubrum and T. mentagrophytes. They also used individuals with althletes foot. The protein was purified from T. tonsurans, characterized with N-terminal sequencing. It was used as a target for IgE in ELISA and RAST. Six of nine individuals with immediate hypersensitivity had SPT positive responses to Tri t 4 (= Tri m 4).    See also Trichophyton 2, as well as Trichophyton 4 (a different protein, but probably involved in the same reactions.
